summary: Two things this turn. First, the repeat of the fixed extended-window experiment (CheckRun f8a32ad3a4de41538ef20a142ae947bc, exit 0) reproduced the full pattern independently, so I recorded an updated interpretation for the VerifyLeader question citing both executions of that fixed experiment with joint_history: nil at 0ms, nil again at 4928ms while a competing node already led and the answering leader was still Leader under a 20s lease, that competitor's write at index 5 absent from the old leader's FSM (still Leader, applied 3), and the control losing leadership at 20007ms after the lease. All four comparisons hold in both receipts, the gap answer is unchanged and now independently sampled, and the counterevidence and limits are restated honestly. Second, that repeat again reported the demoted node's own view as still old (two of two runs of that harness), while the discriminating experiment on the same executor showed no lag and a local run of the retained harness with added per-node sampling also showed the peer already converged - the remaining structural difference is that the extended harness demotes immediately after the leader is elected, before followers have appended the bootstrap configuration and no-op. Submitted that as a successor experiment for the lag question (previous_id = dab6e999e7564b219f604cde213405f7-experiment) adding an immediate-demotion case with the same 20ms per-node view and index sampling, whose predicates separate a delivery stall (view old, LastIndex short of the configuration index) from an entry-processing gap.
